name: Work Permit (New)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a signed employment contract with an employer holding a valid trade license.

Employer must publish a full-page advertisement in two newspapers or reputable online outlets, consecutively for 2 weeks, and submit a cover letter to the Labour Commissioner explaining the hiring necessity together with correspondence/resumes from unsuccessful BVIslander/Belonger applicants and reasons for their rejection.

Requires verified degrees, diplomas, or certifications relevant to the job (translated into English if issued abroad in another language), plus any profession-specific credential (e.g. PADI certification for divers, medical/nursing council registration).

evidence_required.document: Two weeks of consecutive newspaper/online job advertisements
Cover letter to the Labour Commissioner and records of rejected local applicants
Employer's valid trade license (and incorporation documents for new companies)
Passport photo, passport signature page copy

outcome.duration_length: not specified in the sources reviewed; renewable via a separate renewal work permit application

sources.title: Government of the Virgin Islands -- Checklist of Requirements: New Work Permit Application: labour-market-test advertising rule, Labour Commissioner cover letter, employer and employee document lists, $50 fee

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the British Virgin Islands' initial build. work_rights is 'restricted' (tied to the specific certified employer and job description). A self-employed variant (Application for Self-Employed Work Permit) and a Temporary Work Permit variant also exist per the forms located on bvi.gov.vg, but were not independently reviewed for their own distinct criteria in this pass -- flagged as a gap rather than assumed identical to this standard employer-sponsored route. No permit duration was found on the checklist itself; a separate Renewal Work Permit Application form confirms the permit is renewable. leads_to_pr/pr_after_months (120 months) reflects the Residence Status route's 10-year continuous-residence threshold (see vg_residence_status.json), the ordinary route a work-permit holder would use to settle permanently.
